newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman increases gas reserves estimates.
newsitem.headline: Oman increases gas reserves estimates.

text.p: Oman's "expected" natural gas reserves currently stand at 25 trillion cubic feet and could rise to as much as 40 trillion cubic feet by the turn of the decade, an Omani energy official said on Sunday.

"It looks sure that at the beginning of the next century expected reserves will rise to between 35 and 40 trillion cubic feet," Salem bin Mohammad bin Shaaban, chairman of the board at Oman LNG LLC said.
Proven gas reserves stood at 17 trillion cubic feet, said bin Shaaban. The last official estimate was 16.2 trillion.
Gas reserves are crucial to Oman's plans to diversify its oil-dominated economy through gas-related export projects.
Projects for a liquefied natural gas (LNG) plant and fertiliser, petrochemical, aluminium and power projects which will use gas as their feedstock are all being pursued.
Plans to export Omani gas to India and the United Arab Emirates through long-distance pipelines have been delayed by concerns over the size of Oman's gas resource base.
Bin Shaaban was speaking at a ceremony which committed foreign banks and export credit agencies to arranging $2 billion in loans for the downstream part of its LNG project.
The $6 billion LNG project near the eastern Omani coastal town of Sur would boost Oman's oil and gas revenues by 18 percent a year, Shaaban said.
Sales from the plant, which are scheduled to begin to South Korea in 2000, would also contribute 10 percent to Oman's GDP.
Oman relies on oil for over 75 percent of its revenue.
